claims.text: Atomic-size and electronegativity mismatches induce local lattice distortions in solid-solution high-entropy alloys.
The magnitude of local lattice distortion governs the superconducting transition and behavior of the proposed HEA.
Local lattice distortions modulate the phonon spectrum and the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Distortion-induced changes in phonons and electronic density of states tune electron-phonon coupling and therefore Tc.
The starting material is a non-Nb-Ta, non-Ti-rich, disordered, single-phase solid-solution HEA containing at least five roughly equiatomic principal elements.
Substituting a component with a chemically similar but differently sized element can systematically alter atomic-size mismatch while approximately preserving carrier density.
Variations in atomic radii are associated with static lattice distortion in solid-solution HEAs.
Atomic-size mismatch δ and electronegativity differences can be used to quantify local lattice distortion.
Increasing lattice distortion softens selected phonon modes.
Phonon softening caused by distortion enhances electron-phonon coupling up to an optimal distortion level.
Excessively high lattice distortion can increase scattering enough to degrade superconductivity.
Increasing distortion toward its optimum will raise Tc and/or the superconducting volume fraction relative to the starting HEA.
Reducing lattice distortion will lower Tc relative to the starting HEA.
Tc will depend non-monotonically on lattice distortion and peak at an intermediate distortion level.
Keeping valence electron count nearly invariant allows Tc changes to be attributed primarily to lattice distortion rather than gross changes in electron density.
The hypothesis is restricted to chemically homogeneous, single-phase solid solutions in which every element remains at or above 5 atomic percent.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening and atomic-radius distribution metrics can quantify the relevant lattice distortion.
A lack of a reproducible non-monotonic correlation between measured distortion and Tc would falsify the hypothesis.
